newsitem.title: FRANCE: French debt to fall once public deficit down - paper.
newsitem.headline: French debt to fall once public deficit down - paper.

text.p: France's debt will start falling once its total public deficit declines to two percent of gross domestic product (GDP), Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure told newspaper La Tribune in an interview published on Thursday.
"We have to get below three percent. It is only when we have a deficit of two percent of gross domestic (product), in the case of France, that debt will start to fall," he said.
Finance minister Jean Arthuis said on Wednesday the public deficit would fall to 4.1 percent of GDP in 1996, slightly above the government's target of four percent.
